instrument: The probe handed to this bench ran `check --json` WITHOUT `--strict`, and `computeVerdict` only calls `judgeGated` — and therefore `evidenceReport` and the ADR-0020 signature screen — inside `if (opts.strict)` (src/lib/verdict.ts:249). Measured here before the correction arrived: 22/22 `no observable difference` on the self-gate, and the payload was 2654 bytes against 4449 with `--strict`. That reading was blindness, not innocence. Every verdict in this file was measured with the corrected probe (`--strict` in gateArgs, synced from the main repository on 2026-08-20) and with scripts/sig-probe-detail.mjs, which is the same measurement plus a diff of the `conformance` array so the observation can be written down rather than merely counted.
probeMissions: BASE, common to both missions: `node dist/cli.js init --yes --example` on runward 0.36.0 in an empty directory (that tree is green under `check --strict`). Then, per probe row: one house rule `runward/rules/<id>.md` whose frontmatter is `impact: MEDIUM` and `signature: <the shape>` and which declares NO phase (so no other pass looks at it — corpus divergence reports an unwritten rule only when it declares a gated phase at CRITICAL/HIGH, and the baseline confirms it: every conformance entry on the battery mission comes from a probe row, none from the corpus); one fixture `code/probe/<id>.txt` holding the content the compiled regex would run against; one row `| <id> | applied | file:code/probe/<id>.txt |` appended to the Rule conformance table of `runward/architecture.md`, immediately above `## 5. What stays open`. Builder kept at scripts/build-sig-mission.mjs. Runner: `node scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function unsafeSignature --mission <dir> --ledger reports/mutation/probe-mission.jsonl`.

MISSION A — 'battery', 34 signed probe rules, fixtures chosen so an ACCEPTED regex returns immediately: every difference is then a message or a count, fast and attributable to one row. MISSION B — 'teeth', 2 signed rules, adversarial fixtures: the content does NOT match and is long enough that a regex the screen should have refused backtracks. t01 `([)a]+)+$` → `)a` repeated 30 times then `!` (61 characters); t02 `(a{2,})+$` → 60 `a` then `!`. Baseline: exit 1, 2 conformance entries, 222–229 ms. A second reading of t02 was taken with the fixture lengthened to 68 `a` then `!` (69 characters) — the pristine gate still answers in 222 ms.

SEARCH AIDS (design only, never a verdict — ADR-0046 decision 3). The shapes above were not guessed: scripts/sig-exhaustive.mjs, sig-structured.mjs and sig-structured2.mjs apply each mutant to dist/lib/evidence.js and diff `unsafeSignature`'s answer against the pristine one over, respectively, an exhaustive alphabet sweep (up to 48 427 560 strings per mutant), 1 414 878 regex-shaped strings, and 623 980 candidates filtered to VALID ECMAScript regexes. The last filter is what separates a mutant that only swaps one refusal message for another from a mutant that moves the gate between refusing and compiling. Every shape they proposed was then put into a real mission and judged by `runward check --strict --json`.
sideFindings: The instrument, restated because it decides how much of this bench's history is usable: on 2026-08-20, before the correction, the sanctioned probe reported 22/22 `no observable difference` for this function against the self-gate. With `--strict` the same 22 mutants still report 22/22 identical on the self-gate — runward's own mission carries exactly one signature (`assertGrounded|GroundingError|fail[-\s]?closed`) and every mutant judges it the same — but 13/22 become observable the moment a mission carries signatures with shapes. Two different reasons for the same zero, and only the second is honest. The self-gate cannot instruct this function at all.

RWD-2026-0011 says the collapse loop 'was entered by no fixture and could be deleted with the suite still green'. That is now only half true: the loop has fixtures (test/unit/evidence-signature.test.js), and this bench confirms they bite — but they bite the loop's BODY. Its group-prefix branch `(?:\?[:=!]|\?<[^>]*>)?` is still unguarded in all three places it appears (lines 202, 204, 213): six of the twenty-two survivors live there, and every one of them changes what the gate prints without changing whether it refuses.

Nine survivors of twenty-two are the same equivalence class, and it is worth naming rather than counting: the tail `([+*?]|\{\d+(?:,\d*)?\})?` of the collapse pattern captures a quantifier only to write it back unchanged (`${q ?? ""}`). Six mutants of that tail (lines 213) and the two collapse marks (line 217) and the fixpoint break (line 218) cannot move the output. Stryker will keep producing them on every run; the register should say so once rather than re-instruct them.

The screen refuses `(a{2})+` and `(a{2,3})+`, which are bounded and cannot backtrack catastrophically. That is the conservative false positive ADR-0020 declares and accepts, and it is load-bearing here: mutant #7 is visible precisely because it stops refusing them. A future tightening that made the screen exact on brace quantifiers would silence three of this bench's observations, and should land with its own fixtures.

verdicts.argument: The mutated group is the OPTIONAL, TERMINAL tail `([+*?]|\{\d+(?:,\d*)?\})?` of the collapse pattern, and its capture is re-emitted verbatim by `${q ?? ""}` in the replacement. Two consequences, and together they close the case. (1) Because the tail is optional and sits last, it can never decide whether — or where — a match occurs: `String.replace` takes the leftmost position at which the rest of the pattern matches, and the rest of the pattern is unchanged. Widening or narrowing the tail only decides whether one further run of characters is CONSUMED by the match or LEFT standing in the string. (2) Whatever it consumes, it puts back unchanged: `q` is either exactly the consumed text or `undefined` with nothing consumed, and `${q ?? ""}` writes exactly that text back at exactly that position. So `next` is byte-identical under this mutation for every input, and `next` is the loop's only state — `t`, the flat scan and the return value all derive from it. The other capture the replacement reads, `body`, belongs to `([^()]*)`, which the mutation does not touch. No mission can distinguish a transformation that produces the same string.

verdicts.argument: The mutation substitutes the literal `Stryker was here!` for an empty string inside the collapse replacement, so the string the loop builds does change. What cannot change is any predicate applied to it. That literal contains no `(`, no `)`, and none of `+`, `*`, `{`, `}`, `|`. Everything downstream is one of three readers: `NESTED` and `ALT`, whose only obligations outside `[^()]*` are `[+*}]`, `\|`, `[+*{]`, `\(` and `\)`; the collapse pattern itself, whose body class is `[^()]*`; and `/[+*}]/.test(body)`. Characters that belong to `[^()]` and to none of those sets are absorbed by an unanchored, backtracking `[^()]*` — they can neither satisfy an obligation that was unsatisfied nor break a match that held, since `*` may always give the characters back. And because the literal introduces no parenthesis, it adds no group: the loop peels the same number of levels and meets the `i < 20` budget at the same depth. The inserted text is therefore inert for every scan the function performs, on every input.

verdicts.argument: `if (next === t) break` is the loop's fixpoint test, and the mutation only removes the early exit; the loop stays bounded by `i < 20`, so it cannot run forever. Take the iteration where the guard holds. `next === t`, so `t = next` is a no-op and the following `if (flat(t)) return true` is evaluated on a value that has already been judged: on the previous iteration for any iteration after the first, and on `norm` itself — by `if (flat(norm) || flat(source)) return true`, before the loop — for the first. In both cases the judgment was `false`, because a `true` would already have returned. Every iteration the mutant adds therefore re-evaluates a decided predicate on an unchanged string, and the loop still falls out of the bottom to `return false`.
